parsed.explanation: The quoted dichotomy presupposes g(x) >= 0 for all x, but the write-up never establishes this: §1 only notes g(x) > -x (positivity of f), and §2 only yields (7)/(8), none of which excludes negative values. The premise 'V contains at most one positive number' permits V = {-d}, {-d,0}, or {-d,c}, so 'Consequently, either (i) or (ii)' does not follow. The gap propagates: Lemma 1 uses 'b = g(z) in {0,c}' and §7 concludes g is constant, both relying on the unproven dichotomy. The objector's repair is valid: g(x0) = -d < 0 with (4) gives g(x0 - nd) = -d and x0 - nd = f(x0-(n-1)d) > 0 for all n, impossible for n > x0/d. Since this case is handled nowhere in the text, the necessity argument is incomplete as written.
